Pemoving traffic from the local arterial system and putting it on the freeway system will reduce accidents significantly.
SEWRPC's Regional Land Use - Transportation Plan for 1990 and the Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway System Plan are actively being used for the development of all transportation system improvements in Milwaukee County and City of Milwaukee. Improvements to the local streets and arterial highways, as an alternative to the proposal, would be in direct conflict with these plans. Additional reconstruction of this system would be required to provide the same level of regional transportation service on the arterial street and highway network that was originally provided with the proposal of the Airport Spur.
The potential application for modified rapid transit service to General Mitchell Field was extremely limited because of the wide diversity of origins or destinations in the outlying sections of Metropolitan Milwaukee and the automobile flexibility and convenience. The Regional Land Use-Transportation Plans clearly established that a fixed rail rapid transit system would be inferior to the more flexible and economical bus modified rapid transit system and no further consideration would be given to other forms of rapid transit. Without the direct connection of the Airport Spur freeway, it would be difficult, if not impossible, to develop effective modified rapid transit service to the airport and surrounding neighborhood. Projected traffic volumes will not support an exclusive bus lane nor shuttle bus operation.
